transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve seen a deterioration of values.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think for a while as a nation we condoned those things we should have condemned.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: For a while, as I recall, it even seems to me that there was talk of legalizing or decriminalizing marijuana and other drugs, and I think that’s all wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve seen a deterioration in values, and one of the things that I think we should do about it in terms of cause is to instill values into the young people in our schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We got away, we got into this feeling that value- free education was the thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t believe that at all I do believe there are fundamental rights and wrongs as far as use.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, of course, as far as the how we make it better, yes, we can do better on interdiction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to do a lot better on education, and we have to do, be tougher on those who commit crimes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to get after the users more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We have to change this whole culture.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You know, I saw a movie – “Crocodile Dundee.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” And I saw the cocaine scene treated with humor, as though this was a humorous little incident.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s bad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Everybody ought to be in this thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Entertainment industry, people involved in the schools, education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it isn’t a Republican or a Democrat or a liberal problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we have got to instill values in these young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I have put forward a many-point drug program that includes what I would do as president of the United States; in terms of doing better on interdiction; and in terms of better in the neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I think we’re all in this together, and my plea to the American people is values in the schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I agree with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush that values are important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But it’s important that our leaders demonstrate those values from the top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That means those of us who are elected to positions of political leadership have to reflect those values ourselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Here we are with a government that’s been dealing with a drug-running Panamanian dictator.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve been dealing with him; he’s been dealing drugs to our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Governors like me and others have been trying to deal with the consequences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I remember being in a high school in my own state as we were organizing something we call the Governor’s Alliance Against Drugs, and a young 16 year old girl coming up to me, desperate, addicted, dependent, saying, Governor, I need help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re providing that young woman with help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I want to be a president of the United States who makes sure that we never again do business with a drug-running Panamanian dictator, that we never again funnel aid to the contras through convicted drug dealers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Values begin at the top, in the White House.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Those are the values I want to bring to the presidency and to the White House beginning in January of 1989.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m saying that those of us who are elected to positions of political leadership, Jim, have a special responsibility, not only to come up with programs, and I have outlined in detail the very important, very strong program of enforcement as well as drug education prevention.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush is right – the two go hand in hand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But if our government itself is doing business with people who we know are engaged in drug profiteering and drug trafficking, if we don’t understand that that sends out a very, very bad message to our young people, it’s a little difficult for me to understand just how we can reach out to that youngster that I talked about and to young people like her all over the country, and say to them we want to help you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ve outlined in great detail a program for being tough on enforcement at home and abroad, doubling the number of drug enforcement agents, having a hemispheric summit soon after the 20th of January when we bring our democratic neighbors and allies together here in this hemisphere and go to work together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But we also have to take demand seriously.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: You know, we have five percent of the world’s population in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re consuming 50 percent of the world’s cocaine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Doing better in the neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.text: But I think we’re all in this together, and my plea to the American people is values in the schools.
