transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And in my state I’m proud to say we’ve organized a drug education and prevention program which the Federal Drug Enforcement Administration says is a model for the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’re helping youngsters; we’re reaching out to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we’re beginning with drug education and prevention beginning in the early elementary grades in every elementary school in our state, and that’s the kind of effort we need in every elementary school in the United States of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to begin early, in the first, second and third grade, before our youngsters begin to experiment with these very, very dangerous substances.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I guess the question I would ask of Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush is how we instill those values, how we create this environment for the drug free schools that we want in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: If he or representatives of the administration are either with or involving people like Noriega in our foreign policy, or don’t pursue that connection in a way that makes it possible for us to cut it off and to be an example to our kids all over the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the other day my opponent was given a briefing by the CIA.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I asked for and received the same briefing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am very careful in public life about dealing with classified information.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And what I’m about to say is unclassified.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Seven administrations were dealing with Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Noriega.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was the Reagan-Bush administration that brought this man to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And as the governor of Massachusetts knows, there was no evidence that governor – that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Noriega was involved in drugs, no hard evidence until we indicted him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I think it’s about time we get this Noriega matter in perspective.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Panama is a friendly country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I went down there and talked to the president of Panama about cleaning up their money laundering, and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Noriega was there, but there was no evidence at that time, and when the evidence was there, we indicted him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we want to bring him to justice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so call off all those pickets out there that are trying to tear down seven different administrations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I’ve been very specific about those, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And let me lay out for you my own strategy for bring that deficit down, because as a chief executive that’s balanced ten budgets in a row, I’ve had to make those tough decisions and those tough choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: First, I’ve suggested that there are certain weapons systems which we don’t need and we can’t afford.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush has been critical of me for that, but I think those are the kinds of tough choices you have to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’ve also suggested that there are weapons systems that we should proceed on, and I’ve outlined those in detail.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Secondly, we’ve got to invest in economic growth in this country, in every part of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Building that kind of growth expands revenues and helps to bring down that deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Thirdly, we have to bring interest rates down, and we will as we come up with a good, solid plan with the Congress for bringing that deficit down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And, finally, we’ve got to go out there and collect billions and billions of dollars in taxes owed that aren’t being paid to this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s very unfair to the average taxpayer who pays his taxes and pays them on time to permit these monies to go uncollected.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’ve also suggested that on the domestic side there are areas where we can make some cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We ought to be able to come up with an agricultural policy in this country that gives our farm families a fair price and a decent future without spending $20-25 billion a year, which is what we’ve been doing under this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We can help people to live better lives, and at the same time save money by helping hundreds of thousands of families on welfare to get off or welfare, and to become productive citizens again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The thing I don’t understand about Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush’s approach to this is how he could possibly be serious about bringing that deficit down given what he says he wants to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He seems to want to spend a great deal of money on just about every weapon system; he says he’s against new taxes, although he’s broken that pledge at least times in the last year that I know of; he wants to give the wealthiest taxpayers in this country a five year, $40 billion tax break.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He also wants to spend a lot of money on additional programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: If he keeps this up, he’s going to be the Joe Isuzu of American politics.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I hope you won’t take my five seconds away from me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I will say this –

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: If he’s serious about what he’s saying, then the only place he can go to balance that budget is to raid the Social Security Trust Fund, and he tried that in 1985, and I think he’s going to try it again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Is this the time to unleash our one-liners?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That answer was about as clear as Boston harbor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let me help the governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are so many things there, I don’t quite know where to begin.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you cut capital gains, you put people to work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: John Kennedy proposed cutting capital gains.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Paul Tsongas, a liberal senator from Massachusetts said the dumbest thing I did was to oppose the capital gains cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s not going to cost the government money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to increase revenues to the federal government, and it’s going to create jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So that’s one of the things that I think makes a big difference between us.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Massachusetts doesn’t have an enormous defense budget, but nevertheless, the governor raised taxes five different times.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That happens to be a fact.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so let’s kind of stay on the issue, and I have made a specific proposal for what I call a flexible freeze.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it permits – economists on the East Coast and West think it’s good – it permits the president to sort out the priorities, and we continue to grow because I will not raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s the Republican Party and my concern to bring it down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And presidential leadership that I want to provide in this area will bring it down, but we’ve got to get the Democrats – Congress under control.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They do all the spending, they appropriate every dime and tell us how to spend every dime.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to ask the Governor to join in getting for the president what 43 governors have, the line-item veto.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He has to operate in Massachusetts under a balanced budget proviso.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would like a balanced budget amendment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the dynamics of the economy – we cut the taxes and revenues are up by 25 percent in three years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So the problem is – it’s not that the working is being taxed too little or the person working out – the woman working in some factory being taxed too little.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is that we are continuing to spend too much.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, my formula says grow at the rate of inflation.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Permit the president to set the priorities on where we do the spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And remember the Federal deficit has come down $70 billion in one year, in 1987.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if we – and the – actually this year Congress is doing a little better in controlling the growth of spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Spending was only up something like 4 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, it isn’t that we’re taking too little – from taxpayer – we’re spending too much still.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And the formula I’ve given you works, we’ve put it through a good economic model, we’ve got good economists on the West Coast, Michael Boskin and Marty Feldstein up there who’s a very respected economist in the – Massachusetts.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And they agree, that if we can do what I’ve said, we can get it down without going and socking the American taxpayer once again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Capital gains, one more point on that, please let’s learn from history.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A capital gains differential will increase jobs, increase risk taking, increase revenues to the Federal Government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I hope all of those Americans out there who are watching us, listening to us and trying to make up their mind about which one of us ought to be president of the United States listen to the Vice President very carefully.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: What he’s proposing after over a trillion in new debt which has been added in the Federal debt in the course of the past eight years, an IOU our children and grandchildren will be paying for years, is a tax cut for the wealthiest one percent of the people in this country, an average of about $30,000 that we’re going to give to people making $200,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Why that’s more than the average teacher makes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had enough of that, ladies and gentlemen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve run up more debt in the last eight years than under all the presidents from George Washington to Jimmy Carter combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a chief executive who can make tough choices, can work with the Congress, can get that deficit down and begin to build a strong fiscal foundation under this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One thing I will not do is sock every business in the country and, thus, throw some people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to keep this economic recovery going.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: More Americans at work today than any time in history, a greater percentage of the work force.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I will do is permit people to buy into Medicaid.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that’s the answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am proud to have been part of an administration that past the first catastrophic health bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in that there are some Medicaid provisions that will be very helpful to the very kind of people we’re talking about here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’ve got to keep going forward without killing off the engine and throwing people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, the answer lies, it seems to me, in full enforcement of the catastrophic program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It lies to me in flexibility in Medicaid so people at the lowest end can buy in there and get their needs covered and then it also – I do not want to see us mandate across the board that every company has to do this, because I really think that marginal operators are going to go say, “We can’t make it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” And I think then you’re going to see that people are put out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: All these programs – and this cost on his – is – was – I saw an estimate, I’d love to know what he thinks, $35 – $40 billion – and it seems to me that somebody pays that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There isn’t any such thing as something free out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It either gets passed along as increased prices or it gets passed along by people being put out of work so the business can continue to compete.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, I think we ought to do it in the Medicaid system.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to do it by full enforcement of the catastrophic health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think we ought to do it by everybody doing what they can do out of conscience.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a terrible problems in terms of flexibility on private insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I just don’t want to mandate it and risk putting this – setting the recovery back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But, George, that’s no answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You don’t like the answer, but it’s an answer.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, no, it’s no answer to those 37 million people, most of them members of working families who don’t have a dime of health insurance and don’t know how to pay the bills if their kids get sick at night.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I was in Houston on Tuesday meeting with a group of good citizens, working citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: All of them with little or no health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: One of them was a father who had been laid off a few months ago and lost his health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Has an 11 year old son and can’t let that son compete in sports and Little League, because he’s afraid he’s going to get hurt and he won’t be able to provide health insurance to pay those bills.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: My state just became the only state in the nation to provide for universal health care and we did it with the support of the business community and labor and the health care community and with virtually everybody in the state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The fact of the matter is that employers who today are insuring their employees are paying the freight, because they’re paying for those who aren’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think it’s time that when you got a job in this country it came with health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way we’re going to provide basic health security for all of the citizens of this country of ours.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, Anne, let me just say before I answer your question that I didn’t know that the Vice President attacked our program in Massachusetts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I hope he hasn’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Because has won the support of a great many people all over the state and I think it’s a model for what I hope we can do across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But when I proposed my plan this past Tuesday, he or one of his spokesmen called it socialized medicine.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The last time the Vice President used that phrase, I suspect he remembers it, don’t you?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It was in 1964 and that’s what he called Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, he was wrong then and he’s wrong now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Let me say this about AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s the single most important public health crisis, single most important public health emergency we’ve had in our lifetimes and I think there are a number of things we have to do including supporting legislation which is now moving through the Congress, which will commit this nation to the resources to find a cure which will provide broad education and prevention, which will provide sensitive and caring treatment for the victims of AIDS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think we have to demonstrate some flexibility and I think the FDA is attempting to do so now in trying to make it possible for new and experimental drugs to be available to people who are at risk at AIDS and I would hope that we could bring that kind of a policy to bear beginning in January.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I would encourage the current administration to proceed with that kind of flexibility where it’s appropriate and where it’s done carefully and responsibly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But we have not had the kind of leadership we should have had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: In this particular area, I think the Vice President and I are in general agreement on what we have to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The special Federal commission made good solid recommendations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think we’re both supportive of them and I would strongly lead in that area as I have in my state as Governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’re on the right track.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The NIH is doing a good job in research.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The Surgeon General is doing a good job in encouraging the proper kind of education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I notice that the Governor did not mention any testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we got to have a knowledge base.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Testing should be confidential, but we have to have a knowledge.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We can’t simply stick our heads in the sands in terms of testing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m Chairman of the President’s Task Force on Regulatory Relief and we are working with the FDA and they have sped up bringing drugs to market that can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you got to be careful here, because there’s a safety factor, but I think these things – and then also I am one who believes we’ve got to go the extra mile in clean – being sure that that blood supply is pure.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We cannot have a lack of confidence in the blood supply when it comes to operations and surgery and things of this nature.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So, research, speeding the drugs to market, testing, blood supply are very important elements of this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Passionless?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I don’t question his passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I question – and I don’t question his concern about the war in Vietnam.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He introduced or supported legislation back then that suggested that kids of Massachusetts should be exempt from going overseas in that war.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s a certain passion that in my view it’s misguided passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He – we have a big difference on issues.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, last year in the primary, he expressed his passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He said, “I am a strong liberal Democrat” – August, ’87.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Then he said, “I am a card-carrying member of the ACLU.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: ” That was what he said.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is out there on out of the mainstream.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He is very passionate.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My argument with the governor is, do we want this country to go that far left.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I wish we had time to let me explain.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I salute him for his passion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We just have a big difference on where this country should be led, and in what direction it ought to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Nothings wrong with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But just take a look at the positions of the ACLU.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But, Peter, please understand, the liberals do not like me talking about liberal They don’t like it when I say that he says he’s a card carrying member.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, if that quote was wrong, he can repudiate it, right here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve seen it authoritatively written twice, and if I’ve done him an injustice, and he didn’t say it, I’m very, very sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t agree with a lot of – most of the positions of the ACLU.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I simply don’t want to see the ratings on movies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want my ten year old grandchild to go into an X-rated movie.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I like those ratings systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think they’re right to try to take the tax exemption away from the Catholic Church.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to see the kiddie pornographic laws repealed; I don’t want to see “under God” come out from our currency.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, these are all positions of the ACLU.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t agree with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He has every right to exercise his passion, as what he said, a strong, progressive liberal.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t agree with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I come from a different point.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think I’m more in touch with the mainstream of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They raised the same thing with me on the Pledge of Allegiance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: You see, I’d have found a way to sign that bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Governor Thompson of Illinois did.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m not questioning his patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: He goes out and says the man is questioning my patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then all the liberal columnists join in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am not.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am questioning his judgment on these matters, or where he’s coming from He has every right to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I believe that’s not what the American people want, and when he said, when he said at the convention, ideology doesn’t matter, just competence, he was moving away from his own record, from what his passion has been over the years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And that’s all I’m trying to do, is put it in focus.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I hope people don’t think that I’m questioning his patriotism when I say he used his words to describe his participation in that organization.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I hope this is the first and last time I have to say this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Of course, the vice president is questioning my patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think there’s any question about that, and I resent it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I resent it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: My parents came to this country as immigrants.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They taught me that this was the greatest country in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m in public service because I love this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I believe in it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And nobody’s going to question my patriotism as the vice president has now repeatedly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The fact of the matter is if the Pledge of Allegiance was the acid test of one’s patriotism–the vice president’s been the presiding officer in the United States Senate for the past seven and a half years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: To the best of my knowledge he’s never once suggested that a session of the Senate begin with the Pledge of Allegiance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush, I don’t question your patriotism.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: When you’re attacked for your military record, I immediately said it was inappropriate, it had no place in this campaign, and I rejected it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I would hope that from this point on, we get to the issues that affect the vast majority of Americans, jobs, schools, health care, housing, the environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Those are the concerns of the people that are watching us tonight.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Not labels that we attach to each other, questions about each other’s patriotism and loyalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see the McKinney Act fully funded.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe that that would help in terms of shelter.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see – when I talked at our convention about a thousand points of light, I was talking about the enormous numbers of shelters and organizations that help.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The governor’s wife has been very active in the homeless.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: My campaign chairman, Secretary Jim Baker’s wife.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This isn’t government.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These are people that care, that are trying to give of themselves.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The government has a role.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is to fully fund the McKinney Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: There are certain army bases that the act calls for that can be used in certain cases to shelter people when it’s rough.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I think that we’re on the right track.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t see this, incidentally, as a Democrat or a Republican or a liberal or conservative idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see an involvement by a thousand points of light.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I see the funding that is required, and I hope the Congress will fully fund this bill.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They gave it a great deal of conscience and a great deal of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’re on the track on this one.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But – and I, look, mental – that was a little overstated it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’d say around 30 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think maybe we could look back over our shoulders and wonder whether it was right to let all those mental patients out.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Maybe we need to do a better job in mental clinics to help them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because there is a major problem there.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A lot of them are mentally sick.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got to attend to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But fully, my short range answer is fully fund that McKinney Act.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, this is another fundamental difference that I have with the vice president, just as I do in the case of health care for 37 million members of working families in this country who don’t have health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The problem, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush, is that you’ve cut back by 90 percent on our commitment to affordable housing for families of low and moderate income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And when you do that, you’ve have homeless families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t have two and a half million, or three million homeless people living on streets and in doorways in this country ten years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to begin to get back to the business of building and rehabilitating housing for families of low and moderate income in this country; housing for young families that they can look forward some day to buy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got communities in this country increasingly where our own kids can’t afford to live in the communities that they grew up in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s an essential commitment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think the housing community is ready.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But it’s going to take a president who’s committed to housing, who’s had experience in building and rehabilitating housing who understands that affordable housing for families of low and moderate income, for young families, first time home buyers, is an essential part of the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And while I’m all for the McKinney bill, that, by itself, simply won’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to have a president that can lead on this issue, that can work with the Congress, and I’m prepared to do so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: This is one of the most important priorities that faces this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I certainly hope not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And it’s all a question of what our priorities are.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush talked about values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I agree with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: What are our values?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Isn’t providing housing for families of low and moderate income, isn’t it making possible for young families, first time home buyers to own their own home some day something that’s part of the American dream?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: You know, back after World War II when we had hundreds of thousands of GIs who came back from the war, we didn’t sit around.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We went out and built housing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The government was very much involved; so was the housing industry; so was the banking industry; so were housing advocates; so were non-profit agencies; so were governors and mayors and people all over this country who believe deeply in home ownership and affordable housing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s the kind of leadership that I want to provide as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: This isn’t a question of a little charity for the homeless.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: This is a question of organizing the housing community.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’ve talked to bankers and builders and developers, the housing advocates, community development agencies, and they want leadership from Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Washington, by itself, can’t do it all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We shouldn’t expect that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But governors are ready; mayors are ready.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Builders and community leaders are ready.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It will require some funds, John.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we ought to be prepared to provide those funds.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But that, too, will require some choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush wants to spend billions and trillions on Star Wars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s a choice we have to make, isn’t it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Do we spend money on that weapon system in the billions and trillions, or is providing some decent and affordable housing for families of this country something that is at least as important and probably more so.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Because it’s so essential to our economic strength and to our future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s the kind of presidency I believe in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And simply to say, well, the McKinney bill will do it just doesn’t do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We need a president who will lead on this issue, who has had experience on this issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s the kind of priority that will be at the top of our list beginning in January of 1989.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think the governor is blurring housing and the homeless.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about housing which the question was.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: When you talk to those bankers, did they discuss where interest rates were when your party controlled the White House?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Ten days before I took the oath of office as president they were 21 and a half percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, how does that grab you for increasing housing?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Housing is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We are serving a million more families now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But we’re not going to do it in that old Democratic, liberal way of trying to build more bricks and mortars.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Go out and take a look at St.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Louis at some of that effort.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I favor home ownership.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see more vouchers.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see control of some of these projects, and I want to keep the interest rates down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They’re half, now of what they were when we came into office, and with my policy of getting this deficit under control, they’ll be a lot less.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But if we spend and spend and spend, that is going to wrap up the housing market, and we’ll go right back to the days of the misery index and malaise that President Reagan and I have overcome – thank God for the United States on that one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: No, I don’t think there is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: There are two very different issues here, and they’ve got to be dealt with separately.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m opposed to the death penalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think everybody knows that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m also very tough on violent crime.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s one of the reasons why my state has cut crime by more than any other industrial state in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s one of the reasons why we have the lowest murder rate of any industrial state in the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s one of the reasons why we have a drug education and prevention program that is reaching out and helping youngsters all over our state, the kind of thing I want to do as president of the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: You know, the vice president says he wants to impose the death penalty on drug traffickers, and yet his administration has a federal furlough program which is one of the most permissive in the country, which gave last year 7,000 furloughs to drug traffickers and drug pushers, the same people that he says he now wants to execute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The issue of abortion is a very difficult issue, one that I think that we all have to wrestle with, we have to come to terms with.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t favor abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s a good thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think most people do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The question is who makes the decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And I think it has to be the woman, in the exercise of her own conscience and religious beliefs, that makes that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, the Massachusetts furlough program was unique.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was the only one in the nation that furloughed murderers who had not served enough time to be eligible for parole.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The federal program doesn’t do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: No other state programs do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I favor the death penalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I know it’s tough and honest people can disagree.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But when a narcotics wrapped up guy goes in and murders a police officer, I think they ought to pay with their life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I do believe it would be inhibiting.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so I am not going to furlough men like Willie Horton, and I would meet with their, the victims of his last escapade, the rape and the brutalization of the family down there in Maryland.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Maryland would not extradite Willie Horton, the man who was furloughed, the murderer, because they didn’t want him to be furloughed again.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so we have a fundamental difference on this one.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think most people know my position on the sanctity of life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I favor adoption.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do not favor abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I haven’t sorted out the penalties.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I do know, I do know that I oppose abortion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I favor adoption.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And if we can get this law changed, everybody should make the extraordinary effort to take these kids that are unwanted and sometimes aborted, take the – let them come to birth, and then put them in a family where they will be loved.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And you see, yes, my position has evolved.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And it’s continuing to evolve, and it’s evolving in favor of life.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I have had a couple of exceptions that I support – rape, incest and the life of the mother.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes people feel a little uncomfortable talking about this, but it’s much clearer for me now.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As I’ve seen abortions sometimes used as a birth control device, for heavens sakes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: See the millions of these killings accumulate, and this is one where you can have an honest difference of opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We certainly do.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But no, I’m for the sanctity of life, and once that illegality is established, then we can come to grips with the penalty side, and of course there’s got to be some penalties to enforce the law, whatever they may be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think what the vice president is saying is that he’s prepared to brand a woman a criminal for making this decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s as simple as that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s enough to come before the American people who are watching us tonight and say, well, I haven’t sorted it out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: This is a very, very difficult and fundamental decision that all of us have to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And what he is saying, if I understand him correctly, is that he’s prepared to brand a woman a criminal for making this choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I just –

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Let me finish.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Let me simply say that I think it has to be the woman in the exercise of her own conscience and religious beliefs that makes that decision, and I think that’s the right approach, the right decision, and I would hope by this time that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush had sorted out this issue and come to terms with it as I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I respect his right to disagree with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I think it’s important that we have a position, that we take it, and we state it to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: One of the reasons, and I first would like to know which programs you’re talking about, and then we could talk on the merits of the programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But, you see, my fundamental philosophy is give local and state government as much control as possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That might be the explanation, if you tell me the program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I do strongly support the WIC program.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think it is good.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think part of the answer to this haunting of these children that are out there and suffering lies in extension of Medicaid, to challenge the states, and maybe we’re going to have to enforce more on the states in terms of Medicaid taking care of these.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But, Peter, so much of it is, gets into a whole other phase of things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The neighborhood, the kind of environment people are growing up in, and that leads me to the programs I’m talking about in terms of education.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think that part of it is the crime infested neighborhoods, and that’s why I’m a strong believer in trying to control crimes in the neighborhood, why I was so pleased to be endorsed by the policemen on the beat, the Boston Police Department the other day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I think they understand my commitment to helping them in the neighborhoods.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And so it’s a combination of these things.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But do not erode out of the system the thousand points of light.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The people that are out there trying to help these kids, the programs like cities and schools, the work that Barbara Bush is doing so people can learn to read in this country and then go on and break this cycle of poverty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m for Head Start and moving that up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve already made a proposal – and yes, it will cost some money.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I favor that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: So these are the combination of things I want, and the fact that I don’t think the federal government can endorse a $35 billion program does not mean I have less compassion than the person who endorses such a program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I must have been living through a different eight years then the ones the vice president’s been living through, because this administration has cut and slashed and cut and slashed programs for children, for nutrition, for the kinds of things that can help these youngsters to live better lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s cut federal aid to education; it’s cut Pell grants and loans to close the door to college opportunity on youngsters all over this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that, too, is a major difference between the vice president and me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Let me just give you one other example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We have a great many people, hundreds of thousands of people living on public assistance in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The 50 governors of this nation have proposed to the Congress that we help those families to get off of welfare, help those youngsters, help their mothers to become independent and self-sufficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s taken months and months and months to get Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush and the administration to support that legislation, and they’re still resisting.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s the way you help people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Being haunted, a thousand points of light – I don’t know what that means.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I know what strong political leadership is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I know what’s happened over the course of the past eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: These programs have been cut and slashed and butchered, and they’ve hurt kids all over this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I said a few minutes ago, Peter, that you could improve the lives of families and youngsters and save money at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Welfare reform is one way to do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: If we invest in job training, in child care for those youngsters, in some extended health benefits so that that mother and her kids don’t lose their health benefits when she goes to work, we can help literally hundreds of thousands, if not millions of families, to get off of welfare, to become independent and self-sufficient, to be taxpaying citizens, and to improve their lives, the quality of lives, their futures, and the futures of those children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: That’s just one example of how you can save money and improve the quality of life at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: In my own state, for example, we now have that universal health care system, which the vice president opposes, I think very unwisely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: One of the greatest barriers to opportunity for a family and for those children is the threat that they mat lose their health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Think about that father down there in Houston who has to tell his youngster that he can’t play little league ball that he can’t go out on the ball field because he’s afraid he’s going to get hurt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And yet, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush says well, I don’t think we ought to expect business to provide health insurance for their employees, when responsible employers, a majority of employers in this country do and are paying more for their insurance to reimburse hospitals for free care on account of people that are not insured, that have to go to that hospital.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So these are the ways that you help families, you help youngsters to live better lives, and more decent lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Were ready to go to work at the state and local level, all of us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I know the private sector is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: People are all over the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But it takes presidential leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It takes a commitment to being involved and the leading.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the kind of presidency I want to lead.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What troubles me is that when I talk of the voluntary sector and a thousand points of light and a thousand different ways to help on these problems, the man has just said he doesn’t understand what I’m talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: This is the problem I have with the big spending liberals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: They think the only way to do it is for the federal government to do it all.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The fact happens to be that education spending is up by the federal government; it is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is not down.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But here’s the point he misses.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The federal government spends seven percent of the total on education, and the rest of the state governments and local governments and the thousand points of lightened I’m talking about private schools and private church schools and things of this nature–are putting up 93 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But the federal spending for education is up, and I want to be the education president, because I want to see us do better.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re putting more money per child into education, and we are not performing as we should.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve gotten away fro values and the fundamentals.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I would like to urge the school superintendents and the others around the country to stand up now and keep us moving forward on a path towards real excellence.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we can do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But itÏ€s not going to be dedicated by some federal bureaucracy in Washington, D.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Of course not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Of course that’s a charge that’s always made against any governor who runs for the presidency.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think it was one of the things that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush said about Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Reagan back in 1980.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Remember that, George?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And yet some of our finest presidents, some of our strongest international leaders were governors-Franklin Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, Theodore Roosevelt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Its not the amount of time you spend in Washington.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s not the length of your resume.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s your strength, it’s your values, it’s the quality of the people you pick.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s your understanding of the forces of change that are sweeping the world, and whether or not you’re in a position to provide leadership to make those forces of change work for us and not against us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The vice president has a long resume.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But it didn’t stop him from endorsing the sale of arms to the Ayatollah.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And we now know that he was not out of the loop; he was in meeting after meeting listening to Secretary Shultz and Secretary Weinberger opposing that, and yet he supported it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: His experience didn’t prevent him from participating or involving or in some way being involved in the relationship between this government and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Noriega and drug trafficking in Panama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He went to Philippines in the early 80Ï€s and commended Ferdinand Macros for his commitment to democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And he continues to support a failed policy in Central America which is getting worse and worse, and which has in fact increased Cuban and Soviet influence in that region.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: So I don’t believe that the fact you’ve got that long resume or had that experience is the real question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The question is values; the question is strength, the question is your willingness to provide the kind of leadership that must be provided.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m ready to provide that leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I want to be the commander in chief of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think it take fresh leadership now, and an understanding of those forces of change to provide the kind of strength that we need, and perhaps the vice president can explain what he was doing when he supported the trading of arms to terrorist nation, and his involvement in Panama and that endorsement of Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Macros.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think it’s just experience that makes the difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s strength; it’s values.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I thought the question was about defense.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The governor was for a nuclear freeze that would have locked in a thousand Soviet intermediate nuclear force weapons and zero for the West.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And because we didn’t listen to the freeze advocates, and strengthen the defense of this country, we now have the first arms control agreement in the nuclear age.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Now, we’re sitting down and talking to the Soviets about strategic arms, and he wants to do away with the Midgetman and the MX, the modernization or our nuclear capability.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: That is not the way you deal with the Soviets.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’ve met Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Gorbachev.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Met Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Shevardnadze and talked substance with him the other day.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These people are tough.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But now we have a chance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I few have experience and now how to handle it, but please do not go back to the days when the military was as weak as they could be, when the morale was down, and when we were the laughing stock around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And now we are back, because we have strengthened the defenses of this country, and believe me, I don’t want to see us return to those days.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: As to Ferdinand Marcos, he isn’t there any more.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It was under our administration that Mrs.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Aquino came in.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But I’ll tell you what I was thinking of.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I flew a combat mission, my last one was over Manila.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he was down there fighting against imperialism.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he had just-

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he just lifted martial law.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And he just called for new elections.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And all of those things happened because the Philippines do crave democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And out he goes.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think it’s a question of eliminating.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I can tell him some I’m against.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: A-6F, for example.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: DIVAD.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I can go on and on.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Minuteman III, penetration systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, there’s plenty of them that I oppose, but what I am not going to do, when we are negotiating with the Soviet Union, sitting down talking to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Gorbachev about how we achieve a 50 percent reduction in our strategic weapons, I’m not going to give away a couple of aces I that very tough card game.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I’m simply not going to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And under me, when I lead this country, the secretary of defense is going to have to make the choices, between how we keep, how we protect the survivability of our nuclear deployment on the Midgetman missile, or on the Minuteman, whatever it is.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to-the MX.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to have to do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s Christmas.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Wouldn’t it be nice to be perfect?

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I hope it isn’t Christmas when you make that decision.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: wouldn’t it be nice to be the ice man so you never make a mistake?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: These are the-my answer is do not make these unilateral cuts, and everybody now realizes that peace through strength works, and so this is where I have a big difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Of course we’re going to have to make some determination on this, and we’re going to have to make it on the convention forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But now we’ve got a very good concept called competitive strategies.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We will do what we do best.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It’s a strategy that we’ve been working on for a couple of years.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: It is going to take us to much better advantage in conventional forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But look, let me sum it up.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to be the president that gets conventional forces balance.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to be the one to banish chemical and biological weapons from the face of the earth.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But you have to have a little bit of experience to know where to start.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I think I’ve had that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, first let me say with respect to the freeze, that back in the spring of 1982 Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush was a lot more sympathetic to the freeze than he seems to be today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, he said it was not and should not be subject to partisan demagoguery because it was too important for the United States or for the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I didn’t hear, John, exactly where he was going to cut and what he was going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I know this, we have serious financial problems in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve piled up over a trillion dollars in debt and the next president of the United States is going to have to make some choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush wants to spend billions on Star Wars.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: He apparently wants to spend billions on the MX on railroad cars, a weapons system we don’t need and can’t afford.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I thought the administration was opposed to the Midgetman.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I thought the administration was at the negotiating table in Geneva suggesting that we ban mobile missile systems entirely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But those are the choices the next president of the United States is going to have to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m for the Stealth, I’m for the D-5, I’m for going ahead with the advance Cruise missile.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think we need these other systems.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I don’t think we need them to remain strong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to move ahead with the strategic arms negotiation process, with the comprehensive test ban treaty and with negotiations leading to conventional force reduction in Europe with deeper cuts on the Soviet side and Senator Bentsen and I will pursue that policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What I think we ought to do is take a look at perestroika and glasnost, welcome them, but keep our eyes open.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Be cautious.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Because the Soviet change is not fully established yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, I think it’s fine to do business with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, so, I’m encouraged with what I see when I talk to Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: — what I hear when I talk to Mr.
