transcript_turns.text: And I didn’t pick him because he agreed with me on everything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: You know, Sam Rayburn once said that if two people agree on everything then only one person is doing the thinking.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The fact is I’ve picked somebody who not only will be a great Vice President, but if, God forbid, something happens to the president, could step into that office and do so with distinction and with strength and with leadership.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I doubt very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I doubt very much that Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush’s selection for the Vice Presidency of the United States meets that test.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Well, I-we obviously have a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I believe it does meet the test.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ll have an opportunity to see the two of them in action in a friendly forum, wonderful friendly fashion like this.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I had hoped this had been a little friendlier evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I wanted to hitchhike a ride home in his tank with him.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But now we’ve got the lines too carefully drawn here.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But you talk about judgment.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, what kind of judgment-I mean, jumping all over the president on his decision on one area of farm policy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: What kind of judgment sense has your chief education adviser now in jail in Massachusetts?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I mean, there’s-I don’t think this is a fair argument.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But nevertheless, I support my nominee for Vice President and he’ll do an outstanding job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think we have to go to work on the problem of Third World debt and we’ve got to assist those Third World countries in dealing with this massive debt which they currently-which they have incurred and which is burdening them and which if we don’t do something about it and assist them along with other nations around the world, we’ll destroy their economies, destroy their future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And at the same time will destroy markets that are important to our farmers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe we need an agricultural policy which doesn’t cost us 15 to 20 to 25 billion dollars a year that it’s been costing us over the course of the past three or four years under this administration.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s going to require good, solid credit policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And thanks to the Congress we now have an agricultural credit bill which is helping and improving the situation with at least some of our farmers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s going to require a combination of supply management and reasonable price supports to make sure that our farmers get a decent price and I think it also is going to require an administration that understand that there are tremendous opportunities out there for the development of new uses for agricultural products, new uses which can help us to clean up our environment at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bio-degradable plastics-plastic-gasohol, which the Vice President has been involved in, road de-icers made from corn products.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I mean, there are enormous opportunities out there to expand markets and to build a strong future for our farmers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: But I don’t think there’s anything mutually exclusive or contradictory about building a strong farm economy in this country and assisting our family farms and providing a good strong future for rural communities and for rural America and at the same time working on Third World debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, Mexico, itself, is one of our biggest agricultural customers, so in the sense that we can work to help Mexico rebuild and expand and deal with these very serious economic problems we help our farmers at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I oppose supply management and production controls.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I support the farm bill, the 1985 farm bill and spending is moving in the right direction.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to expand our markets abroad and that’s why I’ve called for that first economic summit to be on agriculture.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I will not go back to the way the Democrats did it and used food as a political weapon and throw a grain embargo on the farmers in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see rural redevelopment and I have been out front in favor of alternate sources of energy and one of them is gasohol and comes from using your corn and I think we can do better in terms of biodegradable for a lot of product, so I’m optimistic about the agricultural economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: In terms of the Third World, I support the Baker plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see market economies spring up all around the world and to the degree they do, we are succeeding.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t want to see the banks let off the hook.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I would oppose that, but I think were on the right track in agriculture and I am very very encouraged.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But let’s not go back to that-what they call supply management and production control, that’ll simply price us out of the international market.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Let’s try to expand our markets abroad.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I talked in New Orleans about a gentler and kinder nation and I have made specific proposals on education and the environment and on ethics and energy and how we do better in battling crime in our country.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But there are two main focal points of this election.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Opportunity and peace.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to keep this expansion going.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Yes, we want change but we are the change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I am the change.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to go back to malaise and misery index.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And, so, opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Keep America at work.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: The best poverty program is a job with dignity in the private sector.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And in terms of peace, we are on the right track.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve achieved an arms control agreement that our critics thought was never possible and I want to build on it.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see us finalize that START agreement and I want it to be the one to finally lead the world to banishing chemical and biological weapons.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: I want to see asymmetrical reductions in conventional forces.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And then it gets down to a question of values.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had a chance to spell out our differences on the Pledge of Allegiance here tonight and on tough sentencing of drug king pins and this kind of thing.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And I do favor the death penalty.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: And we’ve got a wide array of differences on those.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: But in the final analysis-in the final analysis, the person goes into that voting booth, they’re going to say, â‰¥Who has the values I believe in?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Who has the experience that we trust?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Who has the integrity and stability to get the job done?

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: â‰¤ My fellow Americans, I am that man and I ask for your support.

transcript_turns.speaker: George H. W. Bush
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: This has been an extraordinary 18 months for Kitty and me and for our family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had an opportunity to campaign all over this country and to meet with so many of you in communities and states and regions to get to know you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m more optimistic today than I was when I began about this nation providing we have the kind of leadership in Washington that can work with you, that can build partnerships, that can build jobs in every part of this country, not certain parts of this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: You know, my friends, my parents came to this country as immigrants like millions and millions of Americans before them and since, seeking opportunities, seeking the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: They made sure their sons understood that this was the greatest country in the world, that those of us especially who were the sons and daughters of immigrants had a special responsibility to give something to the country that had opened up its arms to our parents and given so much to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I believe in the American dream.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: I’m a product of it and I want to help that dream come true for every single citizen in this land, with a good job and good wages, with good schools in every part of this country and every community in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: With decent and affordable housing that our people can buy and own and live in, so that we end the shame of hopelessness in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: With decent and affordable healthcare for all working families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Yes, it’s a tough problem as Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Bush says, but itÏ€s not an insolvable problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: It’s one that we will solve and must solve, with a clean and wholesome environment and with a strong America that’s strong militarily and economically as we must be, an America that provides strong international leadership because we’re true to our values.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We have an opportunity working together to build that future, to build a better America, to build a best America, because the best America doesn’t hide.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We compete.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The best America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We invest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The best America doesn’t leave some of its citizens behind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: We live-we bring everybody along.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: And the best America is not behind us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: The best America is yet to come.

transcript_turns.speaker: Michael Dukakis
transcript_turns.text: Thank you very much.
